neighbours.label: the token right after a metal-oxide name in materials/chemistry text (e.g. the '(' in 'iron oxide (rust)', 'was' after 'vanadium oxide')
fire: The pigment is made from zinc oxide (ZnO) ground into a fine powder.
Thin layers of titanium dioxide (TiO2) were deposited on the glass.
The red color of the soil comes from iron oxide (hematite) in the clay.
Electrodes coated with cobalt oxide and nickel oxide were tested.
A film of aluminum oxide (alumina) protects the metal from corrosion.
The catalyst consists of copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticles on silica.
X-ray diffraction showed that the only phase present was tungsten oxide with a cubic structure.
Rust is mostly hydrated iron oxide (Fe2O3) formed in moist air.
quiet: The pigment is made from zinc chloride (ZnCl2) dissolved in water.
Thin layers of polyethylene (PE) were laminated onto the paper.
The red color of the dye comes from beetroot extract (betanin) in the mix.
Electrodes coated with graphite and carbon black were tested.
A film of clear lacquer protects the wood from moisture.
The catalyst consists of platinum (Pt) nanoparticles on carbon.
X-ray diffraction showed that the only phase present was sodium chloride with a cubic structure.
Limescale is mostly calcium carbonate (CaCO3) formed in hard water.

notes: Card top examples: '(' after 'iron oxide', 'ITO (', 'was' after 'crystalline phase observed', 'alpha' in 'hematite (alpha-Fe2O3)', 'and' after 'MoO3'. Near misses keep chemistry/materials text with non-oxide compound names in the same slot.
